title: Aerosol-assisted CVD method for the synthesis of solid particles of t-YSZ-Fe3O4
author: Contreras-Vargas, Heiras-Trevizo, et al.

steps.title: Prepare precursor solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve the zirconium, yttrium and iron salts (see Table 1) in methanol to obtain a solution with a total molar concentration of 0.1 mol·dm⁻³ and a Fe:Zr:Y molar ratio of 60:39:1; ensure complete dissolution of all three salts.

steps.title: Assemble airtight AACVD system
steps.instruction: Connect the three modules—nebulizer, furnace/tubular reactor, and particle collector—ensuring all joints are completely airtight to prevent air ingress or droplet‑cloud leakage.

steps.title: Load solution into nebulizer
steps.instruction: Place the prepared precursor solution into the solution reservoir and the nebulizer chamber of the assembled system.

steps.title: Set carrier gas flows
steps.instruction: Start the carrier‑gas mixture of argon (inert) and filtered clean dry air (oxidizing) and adjust the mass‑flow controllers to 250 mL·min⁻¹ for Ar and 4 mL·min⁻¹ for air.

steps.title: Set furnace temperature
steps.instruction: Program the tubular furnace to a temperature of 450 °C and allow it to reach a stable set point before proceeding.

steps.title: Initiate nebulization and particle formation
steps.instruction: When the gas flows and furnace temperature are stable, turn on the nebulizer to generate an aerosol of the precursor solution; the carrier gas transports the aerosol into the heated reactor where solvent evaporation, precursor decomposition and chemical reactions produce solid t‑YSZ‑Fe₃O₄ particles.

substeps.instruction: Aerosol is carried by the gas into the furnace.
Heat induces solvent evaporation, precursor melting/sublimation, and thermal decomposition.
Resulting chemical reactions form the desired composite particles.

steps.title: Collect, recover, dry and store particles
steps.instruction: Allow the particle‑laden carrier gas to exit the furnace into the collection liquid; continue nebulization until the required amount of powder is obtained, then shut off all equipment, remove the collection vessel, recover the particles by centrifugation, dry them in a desiccator, and store the dried powder in a screw‑cap glass vial.

substeps.instruction: Maintain synthesis until desired yield is reached.
Turn off furnace, nebulizer, and gas flows.
Centrifuge the suspension to isolate particles.
Place the pellet in a desiccator for drying.
Transfer dried powder to a screw‑cap vial for storage.

description: A powdered composite material comprised of mainly t-YSZ and cubic Fe3O4 was obtained using the reproducible AACVD synthesis method. Noteworthy, the material was synthesized in one step, at relatively low temperature (450 °C), and without the utilization of templates or the addition of pH control reagents, additives, and subsequent high-temperature annealing steps. The chemical reaction and the formation of the solid composite particles occur optimally at the established temperature. The performance of the AACVD equipment is very stable, as long as necessary maintenance services are provided. The efficiency of the system in a continuous operation is around 11 ± 1 mg h−1 of particles. The particles exhibited a solid-like structure with an irregular morphology at the surface. The experience in working with this AACVD system and method has been more than a decade. The validation of the method occurs when obtaining the nanostructured powder, with the characteristics and chemical phases proposed at the beginning.
